definition: One of 88 defined regions of the celestial sphere, generally named after a traditional star pattern.
intuition: Constellations are like regions on a map of the sky: saying a star lies in Orion identifies a direction, not a shared physical location.
misconceptions: Stars in one constellation need not be physically close.
takeaway: Constellations organize the sky into named regions.

source.section: Looking Out from a Spinning, Round Earth
